analysis.body:
# Grid Interconnection Snapshot for AI Infrastructure Planning

Across five major US grid operators, 8,372 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million MW await interconnection as of September 2026. This queue volume reflects sustained demand for electricity—both from existing commercial load and anticipated future consumption. The commercial sector consumed 54.8 billion MWh in June 2026, with Texas accounting for the largest share at 15.8 billion MWh and California second at 10 billion MWh; electricity prices in these states ranged from $8.66/MWh in Texas to $27.33/MWh in California. While commercial sales data measure actual consumption rather than data center demand specifically, the composition of interconnection queues offers indirect signals about infrastructure buildout patterns.

Storage and gas resources dominate queue growth in regions where data center activity is documented to cluster. ERCOT's Texas queue holds 438 GW across 1,778 projects, with battery storage at 160 GW and solar at 150 GW, alongside 78 GW of gas capacity. MISO's 300 GW queue across 3,839 requests emphasizes solar (145 GW) and wind (52 GW) with 68 GW of storage. SPP's south-central queue totals 199 GW with 53 GW of storage. CAISO's California queue, though smaller at 72 GW from 265 projects, concentrates 47 GW in battery storage—the highest storage density of any region. NYISO's 319 GW queue is marked by 291 GW classified as "other," a category that warrants clarification from the source.

The surge in queued storage capacity across all regions—totaling over 328 GW—suggests grid operators are grappling with new load profiles that require flexible generation and rapid response, characteristics consistent with concentrated, always-on consumption patterns. Watch whether storage-to-total capacity ratios in these queues continue rising, as this may signal deepening infrastructure adaptation to data center load shapes.
